verdict: Lossless at every batch size: True.
Batched verification saved verify passes in 1/1 multi-sequence configurations (a batch of one has nothing to batch).

Peak sequences verified per target pass: 3.0. A per-sequence verifier would have needed that many passes per round, so this is the factor by which speculation and batching compose rather than conflict.
Wall-clock speedup on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU: 0.40x-0.40x.

Values below 1.0 are not a defect of the composition. The draft runs K passes serially per sequence per round, and this model pair (Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct against Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct) is too close in cost for that to pay.

Note that this is *worse* on GPU than on CPU, which is the expected direction: a single target pass on a GPU is latency-bound rather than compute-bound, so it is already cheap, and the draft's serial passes dominate a larger share of the round. Speculation needs the target pass to be genuinely expensive before skipping some of them pays -- that means a much larger target, not merely a faster device.
So the plan's 2-3x claim is still neither confirmed nor refuted: it is about an 8B-class target, and this GPU has 6.0 GB of VRAM, which will not hold one in fp16.
